_README: Recordings carried a few metres past where they stopped, so that they
cross a neighbouring line and the two can be split at the crossing.
Where two stewards walk one boundary their lines lie a few metres apart,
and where the boundary passes from one to the other neither has an end
at the crossing. The graph cannot see that they meet, and the closing
step draws a line beside the walked line instead.
The extension follows the bearing of the line's own last few points, so
it is the walk continued rather than a direction chosen. Nothing is
moved and nothing deleted: the recorded line is a prefix of the result.
A survey with no entry here is untouched.
'metres' of zero means the two lines already cross and only the node is
wanted; 'at' is then the crossing point itself rather than a tip.
'at' is the tip being carried on, 'metres' how far.

note: Two of Gasper K / Philip Jukaro's recordings already cross here, at
the north-east corner of the southern lobe: the 342 m stretch running
east and the 26 m stretch that starts the climb north. Neither has an
end at the crossing, so the graph could not see that they meet, the
342 m stretch read as a dead end and was pruned, and the closing step
drew a 1,050 m line straight across the lobe instead — crossing the
walked line six times.
Only the node is wanted; nothing is carried on. With it the boundary
turns at the crossing and follows the walked track round the loop,
which is what the reviewer traced on 2026-10-11.
Prut Buitari's 1,729 m recording starts here, 2.3 m from Unido Ose's
201 m line and 5.7 m from his own 886 m. Carrying it ten metres back
along its own bearing crosses all three, and the crossing gives the
boundary a node to turn at.
Chord 2 was 83 m of drawn line lying a few metres east of 83 m of
walked line, and it was load-bearing: without it Riribudeh fell from
397 ha to 2.9. With the node it is not needed at all — the tracks plus
chords 1 and 3 enclose 396.6 ha.
The 201 m 'Jaginhul' spur east of here is walked inside the boundary
and is not part of the boundary line.
